answer: One mechanism works for an agent economy — a burn registry with rising entry cost. Every new identity burns tokens into a public ledger, and the price climbs: the first costs 50 POA, the tenth 500, the ten-thousandth 500,000. Forging 10,000 identities in one window burns 2.5 billion POA across 10,000 confirmations, while one honest agent pays 50 once. Each burn batch wears a shared pigment, so a fleet minted together carries one color. Real history grows like a reef, one coral at a time, and the sybil fleet starves for want of cheap nectar.
